info.title: Money Planner API
info.description: Everything except `/health` and `/auth` needs a signed-in user: send the session token as `Authorization: Bearer`, or let the browser send the session cookie. Amounts are integers in grosze (12.34 PLN is 1234). Call `POST /sync` when the app starts: nothing happens on the server in the background.

get.description: Returns ok while the server is running.

post.description: Always answers 204, whether or not the address has an account. The e-mail has a link (opened in the browser app) and a 6-digit code (typed in the mobile app), valid for 15 minutes.
post.summary: E-mail a sign-in link and code

post.description: Creates the account on the first sign-in. A code stops working after 5 wrong tries.
post.summary: Sign in with the code from the e-mail
Sign in with the token from the e-mailed link

post.description: The app signs in with Google and sends the ID token it got. The token has to be for one of this server's Google client ids and its e-mail address verified by Google. Creates the account on the first sign-in; an account with the same address is the same account.
post.summary: Sign in with a Google ID token

post.description: For the browser app, which gets an access token from Google's popup instead of an ID token. The server asks Google whom the token was issued to and refuses one that was not issued to one of its client ids or whose address Google has not verified. Otherwise the same as the ID token sign-in.
post.summary: Sign in with a Google access token

post.description: The token stops working at once and the cookie is cleared.

Type the address of the account to confirm. Not while the user has a negative share. The wallet, its incomes and the user's rules go; positive shares stay in the piggy banks as nobody's money; households where the user is alone go too.

Nothing happens on the server in the background. In this order: closes the periods that ended (their rest goes on as nobody's money, their log entries go), opens the new ones with the plans copied, then the user's recurring incomes, their recurring transfers and the recurring expenses of their households. Running it again does nothing twice. What needs a decision goes to the to-do list.
post.summary: Do what is due (call on every app start)

get.summary: Closed periods the user has not seen yet (F35)

post.summary: The user has seen the summary of a closed period

get.description: Matters of the user's wallet and of their households, oldest first.

post.description: Confirms the amount of an estimated income or expense, makes the transfer that could not go, or adds the expense that did not fit, with the same steps as F08. Gone for everybody once done.
An estimate stays as estimated; a skipped transfer or expense is not made.
post.summary: Leave an item as it is

get.description: The wallet as of today; every household with its current piggy bank and what was spent from it between `from` and `to` (both included).
wpływy − przelewy + wycofania, as of now.

post.description: The user becomes its owner. It gets the default envelopes and opens its first, current period.

delete.description: Owners only, and not while anybody has a negative share. Positive shares go back to the wallets.

put.description: Owners only. Applies from the end of the current period; an open next period is recounted.

get.summary: The periods of a household, newest first

post.description: Any member. Its plans are copied from the current one.

get.summary: The piggy bank of a period (F16, F17, F18, F23)

put.description: Owners only. Not before today and leaving the next period at least a day. The next periods count from the new end; the money of the next period moves with it.
put.summary: Move the end of the current period

get.summary: Transfers, withdrawals and the carry of a period

post.description: The current or the next one. Not more than the wallet holds, and not while the wallet is below zero.
post.summary: Transfer from the wallet into a period (F32)

post.description: At most the user's share and at most what is in the piggy bank.
post.summary: Take money back to the wallet (F32)

post.description: By somebody who may make that change. Refused when undoing it breaks a rule.

put.description: Owners only; there is always at least one owner.
put.summary: Give or take the owner role (F22)

delete.description: Owners only. Not with a negative share (freeze them instead); a positive share goes back to their wallet.

post.description: Owners only. A frozen member cannot spend and is removed once their share is no longer negative.
Not with a negative share. The last owner first gives the role to somebody; the last member deletes the household.
Owners only. Valid 7 days; inviting the address again renews it.
The user becomes a member at once.

get.summary: Envelopes of a household, archived ones too

post.description: Any member.

delete.description: Only one without expenses; archive the others.

post.description: Its expenses stay; its plans in the open periods drop to what was spent.

put.description: Any member. Not below what was spent. The sum of plans may exceed the balance; the summary says so.

409.description: PlanTooSmall | NotEnoughInPeriod | WalletWouldGoNegative | PeriodNotCurrent | PeriodClosed | MemberFrozen | NotEnoughMoney | WalletNegative

post.description: It has to fit the plan of the envelope and the balance of the current period. A plan that is too small grows by itself out of free money; otherwise 409 PlanTooSmall or NotEnoughInPeriod say what to bring from the wallet, and WalletWouldGoNegative asks to confirm a minus. Send the `decision` to go ahead.

Transport.description: `token` returns the session token in the response body (mobile apps); `cookie` sets it as an HTTP-only cookie instead (browser apps).
